newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks stretch losses at close.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks stretch losses at close.

text.p: Argentine stocks closed at session lows in slack volume Monday, hurt by a sharp selloff on Wall Street, dealers said.
"We were holding up quite well with only mild losses during most of the session, but then Wall Street dragged us further down right at the end," one trader said.
The main MerVal index shed 1.0 percent to 814.60.

"The market was digesting last week's options settlements, but the undertone remained firm, as denoted by the relative strength seen here compared to Wall Street," said Cesar Arruti of traders Allaria Ledesma.
Floor volume shrank to 35.2 million pesos from 52.1 million Thursday, while over-the-counter deals picked up to 88.1 million pesos from 82 million Thursday.
The broad market closed off 0.6 percent, with decliners beating risers 41 to 16 and 22 issues closing flat.
"Today's gains were very selective, with players hunting for bargains among second-line stocks," one trader said.

The day's only MerVal risers were holding company Garovaglio, which tacked on 0.8 percent, textile and footwear firm Alpartagas and carmaker Sevel, both up 0.5 percent, and oil company Astra, up 0.2 percent.

The heaviest main-tier loser was pulp and paper maker Celulosa, which reeled 10 percent. Traders had forecast the stock would tumble after the company Friday denied rumors of a buyout by a foreign firm. The stock had surged 27 percent last week on the rumor.
Other big losers were holding company Comercial del Plata, carmaker Ciadea and Banco Frances, which fell 3.5 percent, 3.2 percent and 1.9 percent, respectively.
